name: Outstanding Wildlife Leaders (OWL) Teen Program
what_you_do: Spend a year as a teen wildlife leader. You work a 2.5 hour onsite shift each week and give at least 100 hours in the program year. You take part in conservation education that includes public speaking.
grades: Not yet graduated from high school
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who have not graduated from high school. You must give at least 100 hours in the program year and come to a 2.5 hour shift each week. You must be willing to give public talks, lift 15 pounds, and walk safely around animal pens.
pay_detail: Annual program fee of $700. Limited scholarships may be available.
duration: One program year, at least 100 service hours
deadline_text: The 2026-2027 application is closed. The next application dates are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: The 2026-2027 application is closed. Email the youth programs team to ask when the next one opens. The email is on the program page.
notes: Youth programs email: youthprograms@lindsaywildlife.org. Lindsay is at 1931 First Avenue, Walnut Creek. The same page describes Keepers in Training (KIT), a second step for teens who complete at least one year in the OWL program. KIT teens work closely with Lindsay's Animal Encounters department and commit to a 4 hour weekly shift. Lindsay lists its wildlife hospital and exhibit volunteer jobs as ages 18 and up. The OWL program is designed for teens ages 13 to 18.
